topic: Why your brain remembers vacations based on only two specific moments

script.title: Why You Only Remember 2 Vacation Moments: Peak End Rule
script.hook: Why do you only remember two moments from your entire vacation?

scenes.text: Why do you only remember two moments from your entire vacation?

motion_action.headline: VACATION MEMORY TRICK
motion_action.subtext: Why your brain forgets almost everything

scenes.text: You spent seven days relaxing, eating, and exploring.
But your brain throws out almost all of it.
Psychologists call this the peak end rule.
Your brain does not calculate an average of the experience.

motion_action.result_headline: Memories rely on intensity peaks not mathematical averages

scenes.text: Instead, it rates the trip by its most intense emotional peak.
And pairs that with the final moments before you leave.

motion_action.headline: THE FINAL IMPRESSION
motion_action.subtext: The ending shapes the entire memory

scenes.text: If the airport run was stressful, your whole trip feels ruined.

motion_action.title: MEMORY EVALUATION
motion_action.highlight_text: OVERALL RATING: SPOILED BY FINAL DAY

scenes.text: To fix this, always plan one incredible activity right at the end.

motion_action.headline: ENGINEER YOUR MEMORIES
motion_action.subtext: Save the absolute best experience for last

scenes.text: Otherwise, you will always end up asking:

motion_action.query_text: why do I forget full vacations
motion_action.result_headline: The Peak-End Rule Shapes Travel Memory

script.description:
Why you only remember two moments from your entire vacation explained by psychology.
Learn how the peak end rule shapes travel memories and how to make vacations feel better.
